evidence:
Procedure (quality-checks.md:33-35): 'ask what the smallest submission satisfying the brief would be'; defect is 'a static page, a single CRUD screen, or a mock satisfies the ask'. Workbook row 7 (Quality Checks D8, same text in Internal Quality Checks): 'Real build work is required; a stub or trivial tweak can't earn the reward.'

1. The ask itself demands a real multi-part build. instruction.md:1 'one commit that posts every change or none'; :3 'Refuse an out-of-date preview, even if a budget was changed and later restored to the same balance ... retry the same operation without paying anyone twice ... including after later revisions, rescissions or a server restart'; :5 'Keep the underlying offer desk working: requisitions, pending offers, tiered approvals, exact equity valuation, signing adjustments, referrals and rescission clawbacks' plus six named views; :9 'Within fifteen seconds of someone else changing the books, with no reload and no click'; :15 'built with Node.js, Express and SQLite ... keep its durable data in /app/app.db'; :17 'seed once, and retain new work on later restarts'; :19 seven role accounts. hireops_rules.md sections 2-8 define integer-cent composition, half-open bands, dual control, ledger-netted headroom, two vesting schedules with calendar-anniversary month counting, 401/403 discipline and atomic append-only receipts; section 11 defines idempotent operation keys, whole-set netting, ABA-proof staleness and concurrent-commit behaviour; section 12 defines the live editor. The smallest submission satisfying this is a server-backed, seven-role, transactional ledger application with a live client; no static page, single CRUD screen or mock satisfies it.

2. It is not a tweak of supplied code. environment/Dockerfile creates /app with only .gitkeep ('touch /app/.gitkeep'), and copies only instructions/ and assets/. The phrasing 'build HireOps into a compensation change desk' / 'Keep the underlying offer desk working' (instruction.md:1,5) reads as if an existing desk were supplied, but none is; the agent must build the base desk too. That increases the build, so it is not a row-7 defect (any ambiguity belongs to row 6). The reference is 2283 lines of JS across server and client, consistent with a non-trivial build.

3. A stub cannot earn the reward, by source arithmetic on the frozen scoring. score.py: 'reward = round(weighted, 4) if gates_passed and floors_passed else 0.0', floors_passed requires functional > 0.05 (scoring.toml [floors] functional = 0.05). Gate render requires real sign-in ('A static login/workspace picture or only a health response is insufficient'); gate constraints requires UI creation of a requisition and PENDING offer read back in an independent browser context ('A static seed response, no-op success message, browser-only mutation or requisition-only app does not satisfy the gate'). So a static page, mock or requisition-only app is zeroed at the gates. For the next weak app up, a login plus requisition/offer CRUD app with role checks and input validation and nothing else, I summed the functional criteria it could plausibly satisfy (hro_raise_role_*, hro_req_create_recruiter, hro_referrer_roster, hro_date_only, hro_date_rejection, hro_numeric_validation, hro_offer_create_validation, hro_anon_read_requisitions/offers/status, hro_anon_req_create, hro_anon_offer_create): 1.824 of 64.404 total weight = 2.83%, below the 5% floor, so reward 0.0 regardless of visual score. 65.8% of functional weight (hro_change_*, hro_desk_*, hro_live_*, hro_whatif_roles, hro_entries_reload) sits on the coordinated-change desk, and all five polish criteria require working coordinated prepare/commit, live update or session resume, so a stub earns no polish.

4. Conforming alternative that could fail: the brief allows 'An initially empty operational desk' (instruction.md:17); both gates accept it (render: 'empty operational collections are allowed'; app_context.md: 'Operational demonstration rows may be absent; prepare your own controls'), so a real build that imports no demo history is not rejected as a shell.

Observation for the owner (belongs to rows 39/42/44, not a row-7 failure): a CRUD app that additionally shows the five composition/band figures correctly reaches about 6.9% functional by the same arithmetic, clears the floor, and could then collect most of the 0.2 visual share (likert, appearance only), i.e. roughly 0.04 + up to 0.2 reward with no approval, ledger or change desk. That app still needs sign-in for seven roles, server persistence and exact integer composition, so it is partial real work rather than a stub, and the 0.6/0.2/0.2 weights and 0.05 floor are template-controlled.

Why risk=true: the above is source reading and weight arithmetic only. raw-evidence-index.json states 'Full configured grading/workload, reward discrimination/ranking and target/Oracle scores are absent'. Its artifacts (hashes verified, bound to the frozen solution bytes) are scripted golden observations showing the reference really works; they do not show how the configured judge scores a stub or weak app. No stub or weak-app run exists, so the 'cannot earn the reward' half of this row is reasoned, not measured. I ran no application, container, checker or judge.
